messages:
mina: FYI I ran the onboarding eval for orion-v3:int6 on the mixed CJK+AR locale suite and saw bracket orientation flips in Arabic spans embedded with Japanese quotes. chrF dropped ~6 vs fp16 baseline on the subtitle set. Repro: `./evals/run.py --suite locale/cjk_ar_mixed --model orion-v3 --quant int6 --seed 7`

ci-bot: CI job `evals/cjk-ar-onboard/2813456789` finished with nonzero regressions. Artifacts: /ci/artifacts/2813456789/report.html

kai: Reproed. Example input + outputs attached. FP16 keeps U+300C/U+300D (Japanese corner quotes) + Arabic round bracket mirrored as expected. int6 output shows the Arabic bracket mirrored incorrectly (i.e., uses the opposite orientation).

andre: Can you paste a tiny example? is this a generation detokenize bug or a tokenizer normalization issue?

mina: small example:
```
# src: "彼はこう言った (مرحبا) "  -- Japanese text with Arabic paren inside
# gold: "彼はこう言った (مرحبا)"
# fp16: "彼はこう言った (مرحبا)"
# int6: "彼はこう言った )مرحبا("   <-- paren flipped around Arabic span
```

dana: hmm. looks like BIDI mirroring got applied after detokenization for int6 decode path. Two suspects: 1) the int6 detok step applies Unicode Bidi mirroring incorrectly (maybe a different unicode lib), 2) tokenization/merge rules for combined scripts produce token boundaries that let the post-process mirror whole groups.

kai: I checked the detokenizer versions: fp16 uses detok v2.4, int6 build picked detok v2.6 (roll-forward). v2.6 includes a "smart-mirror" path that tries to mirror punctuation based on resolved directionality. Could be a bug.

andre: If detok v2.6 is the cause, a fast rollback is easy (force detok v2.4 in int6 artifact). If it's tokenization boundaries we may need to regenerate merges for the quant build.

mina: I added token/dir dump for the failing example:
```
tokens (int6): [5001:"彼", 5002:"は", 3001:"こう", 900: "\u0020", 211:"(", 6100:"مرحبا", 212:")"]
directionality: L L L ON AL AL ON
post-detok before mirroring: "彼はこう (مرحبا)"
apply-mirroring -> "彼はこう )مرحبا("
```

kai: the directionality tag for parentheses is ON (other neutral) and our mirror logic decides to flip based on adjacent resolved classes. If int6 detok resolved the Arabic run as AL and then mirrored the surrounding parentheses incorrectly that's consistent. Why would int6 detok differ? maybe its run segmentation uses different bracket assignment when tokens cross script boundaries.

dana: Customer impact: a subtitle customer reported odd punctuation in bilingual captions but only in a small % of lines. Risk: low-medium but visible. Suggest we hotfix routing for that customer to fp16 for now.

andre: Quick mitigation: add a post-detok pass that re-evaluates mirrored punctuation and prefers neutral orientation when parent run contains mixed scripts. Cheap to add at the routing layer as `post_process.fix_bidi_parens: true`.

mina: I'll open a PR with a failing unit test (example above) and try pinning detok v2.4 in the int6 build to confirm. If that repros, we'll revert the detok roll-forward and timeline the detok fix.

kai: I'll run a bisect across detok commits between v2.4..v2.6 and also run tokenization ablations (preserve/split on paren token). Command: `tools/bisect_detok.sh --model orion-v3 --quant int6 --range v2.4..v2.6`

dana: tagging @oncall-ml. For customer comms I'll draft a note offering to pin them to fp16 until we have a fix.

mina: Thanks all. Plan: immediate routing mitigation + PR to add unit test + bisect. Will update in this thread. :thumbsup:
